title: Perfin specimen · weight is beam power

usage.title: Perfin specimen · weight is beam power

reference.grammar: A type specimen pierced into white card by a laser. Every letter is a grid of holes, and the three weights are three powers: the more power, the wider each hole burns and the darker its scorched rim, so Light, Regular and Bold are one face at 42, 66 and 92 %. The labels are engraved in a deep raster pass. Through the holes you see the dark bed under the card, shaded by the card's own edge. The face and the foundry are invented.

techniques.name: Laser char

size.label: Size
size.note: motif height as a share of the plate

power.label: Power
power.note: beam power in the raster; dose ∝ power ÷ speed ÷ pitch

speed.label: Speed
speed.note: head speed (relative); faster = less dose per line

pitch.label: Line pitch
pitch.note: distance between scan lines; clamped to ≥ 2 device px, with the dose scaled to match

focus.label: Defocus
focus.note: 0 = in focus; out of focus the spot widens and its peak drops

ramp.label: Power ramp
ramp.note: power falls across the raster, to 15 % at 1

overburn.label: Turnaround burn
overburn.note: extra dose where the head slows to reverse at each line end

haloR.label: Halo reach
haloR.note: how far the heat browns the fibers around the burn

ablate.label: Ablation
ablate.note: how far the surface sinks at full char

diffuse.label: Diffuse share
diffuse.note: share of light from the sheet light vs flat ambient fill

cutOff.label: Cut offset
cutOff.note: distance from the motif edge to the cut

tabs.label: Tabs
tabs.note: uncut bridges that hold the part

thick.label: Card thickness
thick.note: sizes the card edge's shadow on the ground in the kerf

gC.label: Ground below · C
gC.note: OKLCH chroma; reduced at constant L/h if it leaves sRGB

seed.label: Seed
seed.note: every random draw in the effect derives from this one number

techniques.implementation: Scan lines at the pitch (≥ 2 device px), at the scan angle. Dose at a pixel = Σ over nearby lines of power ÷ speed × the beam's gaussian, integrated over the pixel (erf): anti-aliased lines at any angle. When the pitch clamps to 2 device px, the dose is scaled by the clamp so the tone matches a finer screen. Firing gate = the motif clip sampled at each line's centerline, softened by the spot along the scan; the head's turnaround adds dose just inside the edges it reverses at. Defocus widens σ and lowers the peak (same energy, larger spot): paler, softer, lines merging. A power ramp can run across the raster. Char = 1 − e^(−k·(dose − threshold)) → an OKLab ramp tan → brown → black, multiplied into the stock albedo (fibers char darker). Heat halo = the dose spread a few px, browning fibers first. Relief: ablation sinks the surface with dose; the tooth is burned smooth; a fine char crust. Lit by the sheet light (grooves catch it on one wall). Vector cut: a kerf along the motif outline (offset) or a tag; tabs leave bridges. The kerf opens onto the ground below, shaded by the card edge toward the light; its walls are charred.
techniques.limits: line pitch < 2 device px: clamped: finer lines alias into moiré on screen (dose is conserved). power ÷ speed > 1.4: char goes black and ablates; line structure survives only in the relief. defocus > .7: reads as a smudge, not a laser. halo reach > 9 px: reads as a scorch accident rather than a mark. kerf > 3 px: a slot, not a laser cut

techniques.name: Paper tooth

scale.label: Tooth scale
scale.note: feature size of the tooth (noise wavelength), not a tile zoom

pers.label: Persistence
pers.note: amplitude kept per octave: the spectral dropoff of the tooth

aniso.label: Anisotropy
aniso.note: tooth stretched along the grain angle. Machine-made paper is never isotropic; 1 = the 1999 "paper" filter look

form.label: Formation
form.note: low-frequency cloudiness of the sheet (fiber flocs); also mottles any ink printed on it

fAngle.label: Grain angle
fAngle.note: machine direction of the fibers and the tooth

fSpread.label: Grain spread
fSpread.note: 0 = all fibers on the grain; 1 = any direction

depth.label: Relief
depth.note: height of the tooth in CSS px: how hard the light can rake it. The slider is weighted to the subtle end.

diffuse.label: Diffuse share
diffuse.note: share of light from the sheet light vs flat ambient fill

fRaise.label: Fiber raise
fRaise.note: how far fibers stand proud of the sheet

paperL.label: Paper L
paperL.note: OKLab lightness of the stock under the sheet light. Below 1 so lit walls, foil and sheen have headroom to brighten; 1 = the white of the page (highlights clip)

tC.label: Fill tint · C
tC.note: OKLCH chroma; reduced at constant L/h if it leaves sRGB

tAmt.label: Fill tint amount
tAmt.note: how much the ambient fill takes the tint (shadows go cool / warm)

mInset.label: Inset
mInset.note: distance from the plate edge to the mask edge

mAmp.label: Edge wander
mAmp.note: how far noise pushes the edge in and out

mScale.label: Wander scale
mScale.note: wavelength of the wander; small = ragged, large = drifting

mRough.label: Roughness
mRough.note: octaves of edge noise: adds fine teeth without moving the large shape

mFeather.label: Feather
mFeather.note: width over which coverage falls from 1 to 0

lift.label: Sheet lift
lift.note: thickness / curl of the sheet: sizes its shadow on the page

mBite.label: Bite
mBite.note: clumped dropouts that grow more likely toward the edge

seed.label: Seed
seed.note: every random draw in the effect derives from this one number

techniques.implementation: Height = fbm at the tooth scale (octaves, persistence = how fast detail drops off), reshaped by the distribution curve; blended with low-frequency formation. Fibers: curved capsules at a count per 100 × 100 CSS px near the grain angle, raised into the height; pits: small depressions. Both also darken the albedo slightly. Normal from the height gradient → Lambert under the sheet light (azimuth + elevation from the light puck). Diffuse share vs ambient fill; the fill can be tinted. The same field is the stock for FX-01 and FX-02: its peaks take ink first, its valleys starve, its fibers wick. Mask = the sheet's cut or deckle edge; the sheet casts a contact + ambient shadow onto the page by the same light.
techniques.limits: relief > .6 px: reads as stucco: the stock-filter emboss look. anisotropy < 1.3: isotropic tooth reads as a 1999 paper filter. tooth scale < .8 px: collapses into per-pixel noise: digital grain. fibers > 30 /100×100 px: felt, not paper. light elevation < 15°: every fiber becomes a hard ridge; ok for a raking-light study, not for a page

pass_order: Laser char · A CO₂ beam rasters a motif into card, one scan line at a time.
Paper tooth · White stock that is not a screen.
